name: The Maison Carrée of Nîmes
description: The Maison Carrée is a small, remarkably intact Roman temple in the centre of Nîmes, southern France, built in the 1st century AD when the city was the Roman colony of Nemausus. Its columned porch and elegant carved details honoured Augustus's young heirs. It is among the best-preserved Roman temples anywhere, and it inspired the Virginia State Capitol and the Madeleine in Paris.
